newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks extend week's record climb.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks extend week's record climb.

text.p: Zimbabwe's share market continued to ignore a civil service strike that has paralysed key government services over the last 11 days, with industrials climbing over 50 points to another record level on strong foreign investment support.
The 57-counter industrial index closed at 5,808.20 -- a 50.11 points rise on the day -- and a 133.03 points climb on the week.
It was boosted on Friday mainly by gains in sugar producer Hippo Valley and Zimbabwe Newspapers group (Zimpapers) which jumped 40 and 80 cents respectively to 700 and 1,105.

"The market is still enjoying strong foreign investment support and some local investors are trading specifically on fundamentals around certain companies. The market is flourishing on these points," one broker commented.
"Both sets of investors are still discounting the strike and I think the market will remain bullish for a while," he added.
Zimbabwean civil servants walked out of their jobs in their thousands on August 20 to press demnads for wage rises of between 30 and 60 percent.
Minings on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange, gold counters Ashanti and Falgold traded at previous levels of 14,500 and 170 while coal producer Wankie Colliery added two cents to 217.
The seven-share mining index edged 0.26 points to close Friday at 1,278.03 -- just 3.37 points points higher on the week.
